overview: Funan was the earliest known Indianized kingdom in Southeast Asia, located in the Mekong delta. Its port of Oc Eo was a major hub for maritime trade connecting China, India and the Malay world, establishing patterns for later Southeast Asian civilizations.

items.text: The port of Oc Eo connected maritime trade routes between China, India and the Mediterranean.
Roman coins, Indian jewelry and Chinese mirrors found in archaeological excavations.
Indian cultural influence evident in Sanskrit inscriptions, Hindu deities and Buddhist practices.
The concept of divine kingship adopted from Indian political models.
Established the Indianized state model that later Khmer, Cham and Mon kingdoms followed.
Archaeological remains at Oc Eo reveal early urbanization in mainland Southeast Asia.

fall.text: Funan was absorbed by its former vassal, the rising Chenla kingdom.
